earnings.title: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
highlights: NEW ORLEANS – Entergy Corporation (NYSE: ETR) reported third quarter 2026 earnings per share of $1.98 on an as-reported and an adjusted (non-GAAP) basis.

quotes.text: We made very strong progress this quarter across customer, operational, regulatory, and financial aspects of our business.
quotes.by: Drew Marsh, Entergy Chair and Chief Executive Officer

outlook: Entergy narrowed its 2026 adjusted earnings per share guidance to a range of $4.35 to $4.45.

items.heading: The terms and conditions of service, including electric rates, of the Utility operating companies and System Energy are determined through regulatory approval proceedings that can be lengthy and subject to appeal, potentially resulting in delays in effecting rate changes, lengthy litigation, the risk of disallowance of recovery of certain costs, and uncertainty as to ultimate results.

Changes to state or federal legislation or regulation affecting electric generation, electric transmission, distribution, and related activities could adversely affect Entergy and the Utility operating companies’ financial position, results of operations, or cash flows and their utility businesses.
prolonged increases in fuel and purchased power costs could lead to increased customer arrearages or bad debt expenses.

A delay or failure in recovering amounts for storm restoration costs incurred as a result of severe weather, the impact on customer bills of permitted storm cost recovery, or the inability to securitize future storm restoration costs could have material effects on Entergy and its Utility operating companies.

Certain of the Utility operating companies and System Energy are expected to consistently operate their nuclear power plants at high capacity factors in order to be successful, and lower capacity factors could materially affect Entergy’s and their results of operations, financial condition, and liquidity.
items.group: Nuclear Operating, Shutdown, and Regulatory Risks

items.heading: Certain of the Utility operating companies and System Energy periodically shut down their nuclear power plants to replenish fuel. Plant maintenance and upgrades are often scheduled during such refueling outages. If refueling outages last longer than anticipated or if unplanned outages arise, Entergy’s and their results of operations, financial condition, and liquidity could be materially affected.
